batchName: Middle Republic: The Gracchi (133-121 BCE) - Easy Batch 1

questions.question: What did Opimius build beside the senate house after Gaius Gracchus's death?
options: A temple to the goddess Concord
A temple to the god Mars
questions.explanation: Opimius ritually purified the city and dedicated a grand temple to Concord, symbol of civic harmony.
questions.sourceQuote: Opimius ritually purified the city and built a grand temple to the goddess Concord (*Concordia*), symbol of civic harmony, beside the senate house.

questions.question: As a quaestor in Spain in 137 BC, what was Tiberius Gracchus responsible for?
questions.explanation: A quaestor was a junior officer in charge of an army's finances. Tiberius served in the disastrous campaign against Numantia.
questions.sourceQuote: In 137 BC he went to Spain as a quaestor (*quaestor*), a junior officer in charge of an army's finances.

questions.question: To which office was Tiberius Gracchus elected in 133 BC?
questions.explanation: Tiberius became tribune of the plebs, one of ten officials meant to protect ordinary citizens. He used the office to push his land reform.
questions.sourceQuote: In 133 BC Tiberius Gracchus was elected tribune of the plebs (*tribunus plebis*), one of ten officials whose job was to protect ordinary citizens.

questions.question: Who led the mob that killed Tiberius Gracchus?
options: His cousin Scipio Nasica, the chief priest
The tribune who had vetoed his bill
questions.explanation: Scipio Nasica, Tiberius's own cousin and head of Rome's state religion, led the attack after the consul refused to use force.
questions.sourceQuote: Tiberius's own cousin, Scipio Nasica, was chief priest (*pontifex maximus*), head of Rome's state religion.

questions.question: Where did Gaius Gracchus plan an overseas colony of Roman citizens?
questions.explanation: Gaius saw that Italy lacked enough land for everyone, so he planned colonies, including one at Carthage.
questions.sourceQuote: Gaius saw that Italy did not have enough land for everyone, so he planned colonies (*coloniae*), new settlements of citizens, including one overseas at Carthage.

questions.question: What kind of land did Tiberius Gracchus's reform target?
options: Private farms owned by Italian allies
Provincial land in Spain and Africa
Public land Rome had seized in conquering Italy
Temple estates owned by Rome's priests
questions.explanation: The reform targeted public land (ager publicus). According to traditional accounts, wealthy families had occupied huge stretches of it.
questions.sourceQuote: He chose a burning issue: public land (*ager publicus*), territory Rome had taken in its conquests across Italy.

questions.question: What did Gaius Gracchus's grain law do?
options: Set a fixed, slightly below-harvest grain price
Placed a heavy tax on grain merchants
Handed out grain free to all citizens
questions.explanation: The law fixed the price per modius of grain. The state would buy grain when it was cheap and store it in public granaries.
questions.sourceQuote: His grain law set a fixed, slightly below-harvest price for each measure of about 8.7 litres (one modius) of grain.

questions.question: Where did Tiberius Gracchus begin his military career in 147 BC?
questions.explanation: Tiberius served under his brother-in-law at Carthage. One ancient biographer claims he was among the first Romans to climb its walls.
questions.sourceQuote: He served under his brother-in-law in the siege of Carthage (*Carthago*), Rome's great rival city in North Africa.

questions.question: Cornelia, mother of the Gracchi, turned down a marriage proposal from which ruler?
questions.explanation: After her husband died, Cornelia refused the king of Egypt and devoted herself to raising and educating her children.
questions.sourceQuote: She even turned down a marriage proposal from the king of Egypt.

questions.question: About how much younger was Gaius Gracchus than his brother Tiberius?
questions.explanation: Gaius was born around 154 BC, about nine years after Tiberius. He served in Spain in 133 BC and sat on the land commission.
questions.sourceQuote: Gaius Gracchus, born around 154 BC, was about nine years younger than his murdered brother Tiberius.
